title: Verify Framework HID→InputSnapshot adapter (ArcadeInputBridge) against GDD Annex D.1; apply stick deadzone
description: Filed from TASK-029's ratified Phase A analysis (dev-t101 inventory, orchestrator-verified; origin: TASK-023 review LOW-2 deferred items). NAMED ITEM (the trust-boundary fix): ArcadeInputBridge.UpdateSlot (Barcade/Assets/Barcade/Framework/ArcadeInputBridge.cs) reads the move action's Vector2 and passes stick.x/y directly into new InputSnapshot(...) with NO deadzone — analog noise of ±0.0001 can mint full 8-way directions downstream because InputInterpreter.ToDirection8 is sign-based (correct for digital sticks, per GDD §1.3/§3.2 the deadzone belongs at the adapter boundary, not in Core). Fix: wrap with the existing allocation-free InputSnapshot.WithDeadZone(threshold) before assigning _snapshots[i]. Suggested starting threshold ~0.15-0.2 (typical analog convention) — final value is a hardware-calibration/design call, tune on the cabinet. BROADER ITEM: verify the rest of the GDD Annex D.1 'Adaptador HID → InputSnapshot' row against §3.2 (the row was flagged 'to be verified in a later ticket' by the TASK-023 review — this is that ticket). VERIFICATION: extend the existing Barcade/Assets/Tests/PlayMode/ArcadeInputBridgeTests.cs with a deadzone case; Framework code is NOT in the fast suite, so the verification leg is Unity-gated (PlayMode run in the next human Editor window). TASK-029's AC2 records the deadzone as handled here.
acceptance_criteria: ArcadeInputBridge applies InputSnapshot.WithDeadZone (threshold serialized/tunable, default ~0.15-0.2) before snapshots reach Core; no allocation added to the per-frame path.
A PlayMode test in ArcadeInputBridgeTests pins that sub-threshold stick noise produces zero direction (and a supra-threshold input still passes through).
The GDD Annex D.1 'Adaptador HID → InputSnapshot' row is verified against §3.2 item by item, with any additional gaps recorded as ticket comments or follow-up tickets.
Unity-gate: PlayMode suite (incl. the new deadzone case) green in the next human Editor window; fast suite unaffected.

comments.author: dev-t101
comments.body:
Implementable-half hand-off. Two commits on master: ef68f61 feat(framework) = serialized _stickDeadZone (default 0.2, [Range(0,1)], [ASSUMED]-tagged tooltip: hardware-calibration value, biased to the conservative end because cheap arcade-stick mechanical slop runs higher than console pads; retune on the bench) + .WithDeadZone(_stickDeadZone) wrap in UpdateSlot (allocation-free struct transform, nothing added per-frame) + read-only StickDeadZone accessor. 7cb45f4 test(playmode) = Bridge_SubThresholdStickNoise_IsZeroedByDeadZone (0.0001 noise -> exact zero) + Bridge_SupraThresholdStick_PassesThroughDeadZoneUnaffected (~0.71 passes untouched) — both through the real UpdateSlot path. Fast suite unaffected: 559/559 before and after. Also confirmed via ArcadeControls.inputactions: every Move binding has processors:"" — this is the ONLY deadzone in the pipeline, not a redundant layer.

AC3 — Annex D.1 'Adaptador HID -> InputSnapshot' row vs §3.2, item by item:
(1) 60Hz fijo desacoplado del render: GAP — ArcadeInputBridge.Update() is per-frame; MicrogameLoopController.Update() drives ticks via Time.deltaTime (variable timestep); the fixed-tick model exists only as Core config (SessionStateMachineConfig.TicksPerSecond) with NO Framework driver enforcing it. Follow-up ticket proposed (spans files outside this ticket's surface; not touched).
(2) Debounce: PARTIAL, already tracked — bridge does zero debounce; InputInterpreter implements DebounceConfirmTicks=2 for its consumers; legacy v1 direct readers bypass it = TASK-029's ratified deferral to TASK-034. No new action.
(3) Diagonales anti-fantasma: SATISFIED downstream (InputInterpreter.ToDirection8 + CollapsedCardinal per §3.2). No adapter action.
(4) Sin buffering entre microjuegos: SATISFIED downstream (InputInterpreter.Reset() on MgIntro entry).
(5) Detección de puesto muerto (45s idle -> Idle status, excluded from that round's payout, not eliminated): MISSING ENTIRELY — no per-seat last-edge tracking or Idle marking in bridge, interpreter, or FSM. Follow-up ticket proposed (genuine unimplemented GDD feature).

AC4 — Unity-gate run list: PlayMode suite covering ArcadeInputBridgeTests (existing + 2 new). NOTE: Framework code compiles only inside Unity, so that run is ALSO the first compile check on these two commits — dev could not verify compilation; any failure bisects to ef68f61/7cb45f4. Surface discipline: only ArcadeInputBridge.cs + ArcadeInputBridgeTests.cs touched; Loop/FSM (rev-t052's surface) untouched.

comments.author: rev-t054b
comments.body:
STATIC re-review verdict (fresh context; prior reviewer rev-t054 died on a usage limit) — diff f32b243..7cb45f4 (ef68f61 feat + 7cb45f4 test): APPROVE-WITH-NITS -> WAITING-ON-GATE. No HIGH; 1 MEDIUM + 1 LOW, both in the test file, neither a gate blocker. Fast suite 559/559 firsthand (changed files not referenced by the fast-test project — genuinely unaffected). Worktree removed.

STATIC-CONFIDENCE (compile risk): HIGH confidence both files compile in the Editor. ArcadeInputBridge.cs imports Barcade.Core only (not V2), so new InputSnapshot(float,float,ButtonState) + .WithDeadZone bind unambiguously to v1 InputSnapshot (the V2 struct has a (int,PlayerInput[]) ctor and no WithDeadZone — no wrong overload). Field/accessor attributes match the file's conventions, C#9-clean; the test file's only genuinely-new symbol (bridge.StickDeadZone) is public+correct, every other symbol copied verbatim from the adjacent Bridge_StickValues_ReflectDrivenInput test. Only Input-System runtime behavior of Set(joystick.stick,...) is unverifiable statically — exactly what the PlayMode gate confirms.

SEMANTICS MATCH: InputSnapshot.WithDeadZone (Core/Runtime/Input/InputSnapshot.cs:69-74) is radial magnitude gating — zero-below (EXACT 0f) / identity-above (returns this), no rescaling, Button preserved. So the supra 'passes through unaffected' claim is literally true and the sub-threshold exact-zero claim holds. Pre-existing Bridge_StickValues_ReflectDrivenInput (mag ~0.72) stays green above the 0.2 threshold.

MEDIUM (tighten before the gate; does NOT need a fix-round+re-review since tests pass as written): ArcadeInputBridgeTests.cs:410-413 sub-threshold test injects (0.0001,-0.0001) and asserts Is.EqualTo(0f).Within(0.0001f) — tolerance equals the injected per-component magnitude and NUnit .Within is boundary-inclusive, so if WithDeadZone were deleted from UpdateSlot a raw ~1e-4 passthrough would STILL pass, contradicting the test's own 'proves the wrap is applied' docstring. Weak AC2 lock. One-line fix: assert exact zero (Is.EqualTo(0f) / .Within(1e-6f)) since WithDeadZone returns exact 0f, or inject clearly-larger sub-threshold noise (e.g. 0.1, still < 0.2). LOW (nit): supra test (:434-437) bounds loose (>0.3 for 0.5) — would pass under ~40% dampening; optionally assert near-equality to the driven value.

AC coverage: AC1 fully satisfied (serialized [Range(0,1)] tunable, default 0.2, [ASSUMED] tooltip, wrap inside the _snapshots[i]= RHS so Core never sees raw, allocation-free readonly-struct transform, read-only accessor). AC2 implemented (two PlayMode tests drive the real UpdateSlot path; discrimination strength = the MEDIUM). AC3/AC4 = Annex D.1 audit -> TASK-055/056, gate is the human's to run.

AUDIT PREMISES ALL CONFIRMED: (1) processors:"" on every ArcadeControls.inputactions binding — the bridge deadzone is the only one in the pipeline. (2) TASK-055: MicrogameLoopController.cs:155-157 drives the sim from Update() via Tick(Time.deltaTime) — variable timestep; no FixedUpdate/accumulator under Framework/. (3) TASK-056: no per-seat activity/idle tracking anywhere — NUANCE: a HumanIdle SeatState enum value already exists (Core/.../Microgames/V2/SeatState.cs:12, referenced in PlayerRoster.cs:21) but NOTHING assigns it — a target state with no detection logic, strengthening the missing-dead-seat framing. Tier tests-after with PlayMode authored-not-run is correct for a Unity-only surface.

DISPOSITION (orchestrator): ticket stays in_review WAITING-ON-GATE. MEDIUM tightening = a required-before-gate rider assigned to dev-t101 at its next break (after the MECH_02 hand-off, before the human's Editor window) — a standalone one-line test(playmode) commit; no re-review needed per the reviewer, orchestrator will static-confirm the one-liner. LOW optional, fold in if touching the file.
